prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 242 Part A, pulsars: dispersion and folding (tranche T4 by D-R10-232-01): the kernel and validation part only
document: PULSARS.md ("Validation contract"), written after this file
committed: before js/kernels/radio/pulsar*.js, the validator, the oracle scripts and their pinned results, the generator's output, and before any dynamic spectrum, folded profile, period, dispersion measure or oracle output of Prompt 242 existed. Phase 1 of the session (reading the roadmap, the register, RADIO_DATA_GATE.md, RADIO.md, the 241 kernel and its thresholds, the variables period module, the statistics kernel and the NANOGrav pack's documentation) preceded it and fixed nothing here from a result. No expected value below is the output of the kernel: every one is arithmetic written in the leg, a value of the world the generator is told, or a bound set by the stated discretisation.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied, a tool not installed) is NOT RUN and says why. No published number or licence term is typed anywhere from memory. The one physical number the kernel needs, the dispersion constant, is DERIVED from the fine-structure constant, the electron mass, the exact Planck constant and the IAU parsec, and the two measured values are copied from a pinned offline reading of an installed library (tests/fixtures/pulsars/constants-source.json, written by tools/pulsar-oracle/constants.py), never typed; the kernel states their provenance. The density of the DM distance is a required, cited input with no default. Every dispersion measure the kernel returns carries the constant it used and its interval; every distance carries the label 'crude; assumes this electron density' and the density; every synthetic series carries its label and truth manifest. A period is never shown without its search range and the trial count behind its significance.

seeds.design: pulsar-242-design (used only to calibrate stated discretisations and to debug; never in a leg)

scope.built: (1) the dispersion delay across frequency, the sweep between two frequencies, the dispersion measure from a delay and the intra-channel smearing, with the constant derived (not typed); (2) de-dispersion of a dynamic spectrum by shifting channels (nearest sample and linear interpolation) with the channel sum; (3) folding of a series and of every channel at a period, the fold statistic with its chi-square significance and trial correction, the period search over a frequency grid with golden-section refinement, and the period with an interval from the phase drift of sub-integrations; (4) the period from the existing Lomb-Scargle periodogram (js/kernels/variables/period.js) on a rebinned series; (5) the dispersion measure: a coarse search by the variance of the de-dispersed channel sum, then a refinement from per-channel pulse arrival times by Fourier template matching (leave-one-out template) and a weighted linear fit of arrival time against 1/f^2, with an interval from the statistics kernel and the single-frequency refusal 'not-constrained'; (6) the DM distance under a stated constant electron density, labelled; (7) a labelled synthetic dynamic-spectrum generator with a truth manifest and a way to take a pulsar's period and DM from a row of the NANOGrav pack.
scope.notBuilt: the pulsar panel (dynamic spectrum through the image panel, the de-dispersion control behind the disclosure, the fold), the lesson 'A lighthouse in radio', the model-page section and instructor materials (a separate instructional PR after Carl's go-ahead); Part B (the timing model, the independent timing reference, the interferometer concept; gate docs/pulsar-timing-gate) which is a separate gate PR; any pack (packs have 0 B of room and every pulse-series row of RADIO_DATA_GATE.md is C, so the generator is the pack, and it is code); spin-down, binary motion, scattering, scintillation, RFI, polarisation, coherent de-dispersion, a blind search over spin-down or acceleration, and sub-bin timing beyond the stated matched filter.
scope.notRun: B6 (a pinned output of a cited independent pulsar toolkit on the same series: none is installed here and installing one is a download; the request is in PULSARS.md) and E1 (an authentic dynamic spectrum or folded profile against a catalogue value: rows P1 to P3 and K1a to K1c of RADIO_DATA_GATE.md are C and the one row that passes, row 16, is a table of periods and dispersion measures with no series in it).

instrument.label: SYNTHETIC PULSAR SERIES: an invented pulsar observed by an invented receiver, with a stated period, dispersion measure and pulse profile, not a measurement of any pulsar. The band, channel count, sampling and every parameter below are the world's truth, chosen round, and no published value.
instrument.note: channel centres fLo + (i + 1/2) df, ascending; the dispersion delay is relative to infinite frequency, and de-dispersion references the top of the band

profile.kind: one Gaussian component, periodic (images at +-1 turn summed)
profile.note: amplitude in units of the per-sample noise sigma; peak amplitude is the same in every channel unless a spectral index is given

subchannels.note: the generator averages the delayed pulse over this many equal sub-bands of a channel (intra-channel smearing); 1 is the exact centre-frequency delay of the analytic legs

periodTruthS.note: invented values; the analytic values are chosen incommensurate with the sampling

instrument.referenceFrequency: top of the band for de-dispersion

analysisRule.name: PULSAR-RULE-1 (committed here before the kernel existed)
steps: S1 inputs: the dynamic spectrum (ascending channel frequencies in MHz, sample time dt in s, a nchan by nsamp array), the DM search range [dmMin, dmMax], the period search range [pMin, pMax] or one period, nbin (default 64), the dispersion constant (default the derived one), and optionally the noise sigma per channel

S2 noise per channel: from the caller, else 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the successive differences of the channel, divided by sqrt(2) (white noise assumed; a signal's sharp edges are outliers the median ignores)

S3 de-dispersion: channel c is advanced by delta_c = K DM (1/f_c^2 - 1/f_ref^2) with f_ref the top channel centre; 'nearest' shifts by round(delta_c / dt) samples and keeps no noise correlation; 'linear' interpolates; samples without data in every channel are dropped, none wrapped; the channel sum is the mean

S4 DM coarse search (needs no period): the variance of the nearest-shift channel sum on a grid dm_i = dmMin + i step with step = (P_guess / 128) / (K |1/f_lo^2 - 1/f_hi^2|), P_guess the geometric mean of the period range (the search never needs the period to better than that), refined by a parabola through the three points at the maximum; refused 'dm-at-range-edge' if the maximum is within one step of either end; refused 'ambiguous-dm' if a second local maximum outside three steps of the first reaches 0.9 of the first's excess variance over the grid median

S5 period search: the channel sum de-dispersed at the coarse DM (nearest), folded at trial frequencies on a uniform grid with spacing 1 / (T nbin 2) (T the series length), statistic chi2 = sum over bins of n_b (m_b - mean)^2 / sigma_sum^2 with nbin - 1 degrees of freedom, sigma_sum from S2 on the channel sum; golden-section refinement in frequency between the neighbours of the maximum; significance p = chi-square survival function, trial-corrected p_corr = min(1, N_trials p) with N_trials the grid size times the number of DM trials; refused 'no-pulsar' if p_corr >= 1e-3
S6 channel folds: each channel folded at the period into nbin bins by bin = floor(frac(t / P) nbin), t_j = j dt; per-bin variance sigma_c^2 / n_b

S7 arrival phase by matched filter: with P_k the DFT (k = 1 .. nbin / 2 - 1) of a channel profile and T_k that of the template, phi = argmax over phi of Re sum_k P_k conj(T_k) exp(2 pi i k phi) (a scan of 16 nbin points then Newton on the analytic derivative), the template being the weighted mean over the OTHER channels, each aligned at the current DM by its Fourier phase factor (leave-one-out); harmonics kept are those with |T_k|^2 above 9 times the template's noise variance per harmonic; amplitude a = C / sum |T_k|^2; per-harmonic noise variance v = (nbin / 2) sigma_c^2 mean(1 / n_b); phase variance (v + a^2 v_T) / (a^2 (2 pi)^2 sum k^2 |T_k|^2), v_T the template's; a channel is used if a^2 sum |T_k|^2 / v >= 25 (signal-to-noise 5)

S8 DM refinement: weighted least squares of r_c = phi_c P (s) on x_c = K / f_c^2 with an intercept, DM_new = DM + slope; four or more used channels, else refused 'too-few-channels'; the normal matrix must have a determinant above 1e-12 of the product of its diagonal, else refused 'not-constrained' (a single frequency, or a band too narrow to separate the delay from a constant); iterated until |slope| < 1e-3 sigma or 5 passes; sigma_DM from the covariance scaled by sqrt(max(1, chi2 / dof)); structured residuals flagged when the chi-square tail probability is under 1e-3; refused 'not-constrained' if the 95 percent half-width exceeds dmMax - dmMin

S9 period interval: M = 8 sub-integrations (equal times), the channels aligned at the final DM, each folded, the arrival phase of each against the leave-one-out template (S7), weighted least squares of phase on mid-time giving a frequency offset s; P_new = P / (1 - s P); two passes; sigma_P = P^2 sigma_s with the same chi-square scaling; fewer than 4 used sub-integrations refused 'too-few-subintegrations'
S10 intervals through the statistics kernel's covarianceInterval at levels 0.6827 and 0.95; the result names the constant, the range, the trial count, the template rule and every flag
analysisRule.assumes: white Gaussian noise with a constant variance per channel; a pulse profile the same shape (up to scale) in every channel; delays following K DM / f^2 exactly (cold, unmagnetised plasma, no scattering); a period constant over the observation (no spin-down, no binary motion); intra-channel smearing treated as part of the profile, not corrected (coherent de-dispersion is not built)

distanceRule.formula: d = DM / n_e with DM in pc/cm3 and n_e in cm^-3 gives pc; n_e is a required input with a source string and no default
distanceRule.label: crude; assumes this electron density
distanceRule.interval: if the caller gives a density range [n_lo, n_hi] the distance range is [DM / n_hi, DM / n_lo]; the label and the density are in the result either way
distanceRule.limits: a uniform density along the whole path ignores the thin electron layer, the arms and local structure: the result is a rough order of magnitude and says so; no pulsar distance is claimed

constants.dispersion: K = alpha h / (4 pi^2 m_e) in SI (m^2 / s), times (1 pc in m)(1e6 m^-3 per cm^-3) for DM in pc/cm3, over 1e12 for MHz^2: seconds times MHz^2 per (pc/cm3). The derivation uses e^2 / (4 pi eps0) = alpha hbar c
constants.source: tests/fixtures/pulsars/constants-source.json, written by tools/pulsar-oracle/constants.py from astropy.constants as installed (name, value, unit, uncertainty, reference as the library gives them); the module copies the two values from it and a test holds them equal
constants.convention: a timing package may adopt a rounded conventional constant instead of the derived one; the kernel takes the constant as an option and names it in every result. Which one a given DM was reported under is a question for Carl (PULSARS.md)

checks.what: the delay t(f, DM) = K DM / f^2: t(f) / t(2 f) = 4 and t(DM2) / t(DM1) = DM2 / DM1 each to a relative 1e-14 at five frequencies and five dispersion measures; a lower frequency arrives later; sweep(f1, f2, DM) equals t(f1) - t(f2) exactly (relative 1e-14) and is positive for f1 < f2; the dispersion measure from a sweep inverts it to a relative 1e-12; the frequency in Hz, MHz and GHz agree to a relative 1e-14; a non-positive frequency or negative DM-range is refused by code

the module's derived constant equals alpha h / (4 pi^2 m_e) (PC_M 1e6 / 1e12) recomputed in the validator from the values in constants-source.json to a relative 1e-14; the two inputs in the module equal the fixture's to the last digit; the module's status string names the source file and says the values are not verified by a fetch

the intra-channel smearing 2 K DM df / f^3 equals the exact difference of the delays at the channel's edges times (1 - x^2)^2, x = df / (2 f), to a relative 1e-12 at the instrument's band (channel width 18.75 MHz) at DM 10, 60 and 120; the ratio of the formula to the exact difference differs from 1 by under 5e-5 at the instrument's centre channel

noise-free series of the analytic worlds (one sub-band, the exact centre delays): the linearly interpolated de-dispersion at the true DM then folded puts the profile's centroid at the world's pulse phase to 2e-4 turn on all six worlds; the nearest-sample version to 6e-4 turn; the fold conserves the sum (sum of n_b m_b equals the sum of the series to a relative 1e-12); de-dispersing at a DM off by an amount whose band sweep is 2 pulse standard deviations lowers the fold statistic by a factor of at least 1.5 against the true DM

the fold search plus the sub-integration refinement recovers the period of noise-free series (the six analytic periods, DM at the true value) to a relative 2e-6; the period from the existing Lomb-Scargle periodogram on the channel sum rebinned to 1 ms-multiples recovers it to within the periodogram's peak width P^2 / T

the DM measurement (coarse search, then arrival-time refinement, with the noise sigma given as 1e-3 of the amplitude because a noise-free series has none to estimate) recovers the six analytic dispersion measures to 0.05 pc/cm3 absolute

on 400 noise-only channel-sum series folded at a fixed period (not searched), the fold statistic has mean within 4 percent of its degrees of freedom (nbin - 1) and the fraction with p < 0.05 is within [0.02, 0.08]; the trial correction p_corr = min(1, N p) is monotone and never below p

the distance is DM / n_e exactly (relative 1e-15) for three pairs; a density range gives [DM / n_hi, DM / n_lo]; every result, at any call, carries the label 'crude; assumes this electron density', the density and its source; a missing, zero, negative or non-finite density, a negative DM, or a missing source string is refused by code ('missing-density', 'bad-argument'); the function returns no distance on a refusal

the oracle (astropy.constants: e, eps0, m_e, c; independent algebra e^2 / (8 pi^2 eps0 m_e c)) gives the same dispersion constant as the module to a relative 1e-9, and the same delays at eight frequencies and three DMs to a relative 1e-9

amendments.what: The coarse DM statistic is the harmonic-summed Fourier power of the nearest-shift channel sum, not its variance. The channel sum is the mean of the shifted channels, mean-removed and zero-padded to the next power of two at or above twice its length; the power is |X_k|^2 / (L sigma_sum^2) with sigma_sum = sqrt(sum sigma_c^2) / nchan; for each fundamental bin k from floor(N dt / pMax) to ceil(N dt / pMin) the statistic is the sum over h = 1 .. 4 of the largest power within ceil(h / 2) bins of h k, and the trial value is the maximum over k. The DM step is unchanged and the maximum over the grid is refined by a parabola as before. The edge and ambiguity rules are unchanged except that the main lobe (the run around the maximum above half its excess over the grid median, widened by three steps on each side) is excluded when looking for a second maximum, so a broad flat top is not read as a second DM. A band whose sweep at the largest DM of the range is under 1/128 of the period guess (step > dmMax) is refused 'not-constrained' before any search.
amendments.why: One design run on the design seed (period 0.2373, DM 60, amplitude 0.5, four sub-bands): the variance statistic had a lobe about 35 pc/cm3 wide, a signal-to-noise of about 4.6 per trial, put its maximum at 65.2 and was refused 'ambiguous-dm' by a noisy shoulder inside the lobe; the Fourier statistic peaked at 60.15. No leg had run; no bound changed.

amendments.what: E2 search ranges, fixed here before any validator run: the DM range is [DM_row - 10, DM_row + 10] clipped at 0 (the catalogue value as the analyst's prior from an earlier observation, which is also why E2 is not an authentic test) and the period range is [0.8 P, 1.25 P] with P = 1 / F0 (an analyst who knows the period to 25 percent).
amendments.why: The thresholds said the instrument and the sampling but not the search ranges; at periods of 8 to 100 ms the DM step is 0.04 to 0.5 pc/cm3 and a blind range of hundreds would cost minutes per pulsar. No leg had run.

amendments.what: The sub-integration slope is multiplied by (M - 1) / M because each sub-integration is matched to a template of the OTHER sub-integrations: for equal weights the phase of one against the mean phase of the others is s M / (M - 1) (t_m - mean t). The standard deviation takes the same factor. This is a derivation, written before the validator ran; B5 compares against an oracle that applies the same factor, and A5 and C2 test that it is right (a wrong factor would show as a period bias of one part in M).
amendments.why: S9 said a weighted line gives a frequency offset s; it did not say what the leave-one-out template does to the slope. No bound changed.

amendments.what: Refusal precedence in the whole analysis: 'no-pulsar' (S5, the trial-corrected probability) first, then 'dm-at-range-edge', then 'ambiguous-dm', then 'period-at-range-edge' (the strongest period is at an edge of the range: the true period may lie outside), then the refusals of the refinement stages. The trial count in S5 is the period grid size times the number of DM trials. A single-channel series skips the DM stages, folds as it is and returns the period with the DM refused 'not-constrained' (status 'partial').
amendments.why: S5 and S4 each said when to refuse but not which wins when several hold; a noise-only series must say 'no-pulsar', not report an arbitrary DM edge (D2). No bound changed.

amendments.what: The period search takes the grid maximum as its period; the golden-section refinement between the neighbours of the maximum is dropped. The sub-integration phase drift (S9, two passes) is the refinement and gives the interval. The grid, the statistic, the significance and the trial correction are unchanged.
amendments.why: Found while checking the kernel's analysis against the oracle's on the 24 B4 and B5 worlds, before the validator existed (so before any leg was judged): the fold statistic is a ragged function of the period at scales finer than the grid, because samples change bins one at a time, so a golden-section search in the kernel and a bounded Brent search in the oracle settled on different local maxima (the periods differed by 1e-7 to 8e-5 of themselves) and the DMs by up to 0.3 pc/cm3 through the period. The grid maximum is the same in both. This is a design change made after seeing a kernel output, and it is recorded as such; no bound was changed.
